A language model learns statistical patterns from the text it sees during training. Careful dataset preparation can reduce noise and improve reproducibility.
The training corpus should preserve document provenance, license details, and stable checksums. Researchers should record every transformation applied to the data.

Validation data must remain separate from training data. Exact duplicates should be removed before splitting, and evaluation prompts should not be included in training.
Text normalization should be conservative and should not silently change the meaning of a document. Every filter should report how many examples it rejects.
Model perplexity depends on tokenization and evaluation protocol. Comparing different tokenizers using raw perplexity alone can be misleading.

When preparing a corpus, researchers should inspect both retained and rejected examples. Heuristics can remove valid text, especially in multilingual or informal datasets.
